analysis.title: Santa Rally Or SOX Crash - Which 1999 Are We In?
key_insights: Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid says that since 1928 the S&P 500's final dip of a typical year has bottomed on October 27, after which it is broadly one-way traffic into year-end in an average year. A midterm election a week away lines up the seasonal tailwinds.

BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky argues 2026 has not been an average year and that none of the coming catalysts (FOMC, mega-cap earnings, midterms, Middle East 'deal' hopes) is a true 'clearing event'. He focuses on the 'reaction to the reaction' and notes the last two attempts at a clearing event went poorly.
Only one of eleven S&P 500 sectors (communication services) has an RSI below 49. On March 31 only three sectors had an RSI above 50. BTIG sees little left to flush.

Options hedging is light: the 20-day equity-only put/call ratio is 0.59 and the total is 0.87, versus roughly 0.67 and close to 1.0 at the March peak. In March and July put/call ratios surged to multi-year highs.

Hedge fund positioning is lighter, but Nomura's McElligott says roughly 100 multi-manager PMs lost their jobs after October's AI growth scare and momentum unwind. Someone bought about $1.6B of delta in Mag7 calls hours before the Fed.

BTIG's 2000 SOX analog diverged briefly but is back on track. It implies a few more days of rally and then a sharp decline into November. BTIG calls this probably the least consensus view. In the 2000 version the SOX fell from about 1,200 in early September to about 540 by early December.

BTIG expects SOXX to fail and turn lower in the 550-570 range, with a likely test of the 20/50 DMA convergence at 516-532 first. SOXX was about $517 on BTIG's chart, and the 200-DMA is near $475. BTIG has little confidence the 200 DMA holds.
SOXX printed a 10-count at last week's lows and is now on a 3-count to the upside. Krinsky expects upside exhaustion in 4-7 days, which falls around November 3-5 (midterm week).
BofA's derivatives team shows defensives such as staples and healthcare in bubble-risk territory, last seen at the dotcom peak.

Krinsky scores Meta and SpaceX as failed reactions: Meta fell as its CDS hit a record on capex, and SpaceX's pop was sold within days. SK Hynix reacted well but came in after a -33% drawdown, so Krinsky treats it as a short-term clearing event, with a possible rally toward $180 before failing again.

FOMC held rates, ending the hiking cycle pause as expected, with Hammack and Lisa Cook dissenting in favor of a hike. Warsh's statement was light and his press conference hawkish, yet stocks rallied. Warsh flagged that rising rates are hurting AI and the Fed is unhappy about memory price inflation, which a zerohedge post says would add 0.5% to 2026 core PCE.

After the bell, Microsoft rose about 6% on Azure growth of 48% despite commercial bookings falling 12%. Alphabet fell about 8% on a revenue and EPS miss, with free cash flow negative for a second straight quarter at -$9.1B.

Deutsche's Chadha and Thatte found the S&P was higher over the three months from early October in 21 of the last 23 midterm years. In midterm years the index typically peaks in late April and slides about 4-5% into an early-October trough. Reid also lists midterm years that turned into bear markets (1962, 1974, 2002, 2022).

2026 is a 'gentler impression' of the midterm script: the S&P closed at a record on May 29 up about 11% YTD and is less than 1% higher nearly five months later. The S&P has been in the same range since late July, about 1% below an all-time high.
The author leans toward Krinsky: one more leg of the bounce into 550-570 on SOXX, then a reversal around midterm week. The bull case holds if Microsoft's pop holds and Alphabet's dip gets bought.

earnings_insights: Microsoft reported 10/28 after the close: Azure growth 48%, commercial bookings -12%, stock about +6% after hours. The report gives no EPS figures.

Alphabet reported 10/28 after the close: revenue and EPS missed, free cash flow -$9.1B for a second straight quarter, stock about -8% after hours to its lowest level since April. The report gives no EPS or revenue figures.
Meta's stock fell after an initial pop as its CDS hit a record on the capex bill. SpaceX's post-earnings pop was sold within days. SK Hynix reacted well after a -33% drawdown.

macro_indicators.reading: Rates held, with dissents from Hammack and Cook in favor of a hike
macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed paused its hiking cycle as expected, but two dissents for a hike and a hawkish press conference lean hawkish.
A zerohedge post paraphrasing Warsh says memory price inflation would add 0.5% to 2026 core PCE, which makes the memory rally an inflation input for the Fed.

tension_points.bull_case: Deutsche Bank's Reid says the S&P's final dip of a typical year bottoms around October 27 and the midterm seasonal tailwinds are strong. The S&P was higher over the next three months in 21 of the last 23 midterm years.
tension_points.bear_case: BTIG's Krinsky says 2026 is not an average year. The S&P is about 1% from a record, put/call ratios show complacency and only one sector is oversold, so nothing is being cleared. The last two clearing events failed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: For the bear case, Microsoft's pop holding and Alphabet's dip being bought by Friday's close.

tension_points.bull_case: SOXX found buyers at its 200-day moving average and the Nasdaq led on SK Hynix-fueled memory strength.
tension_points.bear_case: BTIG's 2000 analog implies a rally into 550-570 on SOXX and then a sharp decline into November, and the 200 DMA near $475 is unlikely to hold.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The analog has already diverged once. The report gives no explicit invalidation level.
